evals.name: board-state-report
evals.prompt: What's the current state of my homelab project board? I want to know how many issues are open vs closed, what the Status breakdown looks like for open issues, how many open issues are missing a Priority and Size, and which open issues are stalest.
evals.expected_output: Runs ghpm.py report. Prints state totals, per-Status breakdown for OPEN, single-select coverage (Priority/Size set counts), and the stalest-OPEN list. Should reference real issue numbers and not just describe the command.

evals.name: triage-set-fields
evals.prompt: Triage issue #437 — it's a real bug, high priority, size M. Set Priority to High, Size to M, and Status to In Progress. Then add the 'bug' label.
evals.expected_output: Uses ghpm.py fields first to confirm legal values (good practice), then runs set 437 Priority=High, set 437 Size=M, set 437 Status="In Progress", label 437 bug. Verifies field/option names exist before applying.

evals.name: link-subissues
evals.prompt: Make #440 a sub-issue of #420, and mark #440 as blocked by #418.
evals.expected_output: Runs link 420 440 --relation subissue (or default), then link 418 440 --relation blocks. Explains that 'subissue' creates a true parent/child link while 'blocks' uses label+body-ref convention since GitHub has no first-class blocks link via GraphQL.

evals.name: create-and-rank
evals.prompt: Create a new issue called 'Upgrade Caddy to v2.9' in the homelab repo with body 'Tracking the Caddy 2.9 upgrade for the reverse-proxy stack.', label it 'infra', assign it to me, add it to the project, set Size to S and Priority to Medium.
evals.expected_output: Runs create with --label infra --assignee <self>, then set on the new issue number for Size=S and Priority=Medium. Note: create auto-adds to project, so no separate add-to-project needed.

evals.name: dry-run-bulk
evals.prompt: I want to move issues 430, 431, 432, 433 all to Status='Todo' but I'm nervous — show me what would happen first.
evals.expected_output: Uses --dry-run in a loop over the four issue numbers, printing the planned mutation for each without sending. Does NOT execute the mutations. Explains the dry-run behavior to the user and offers to run for real.
